name: Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) Usage
purpose: Tracks RDP logons and session reconnections to a target machine, and identifies which accounts were used to do so, purely from the Security log's account-usage perspective.
key_fields: Event ID 4624: Logon Type 10 (remote interactive logon)
Hostname and IP address of the remote machine making the connection, recorded on the 4624/4778/4779 events
normal_baseline: RDP account usage aligns with known admin jump-box or approved remote-work sources, at expected times and from expected source hosts.
anomalies: Logon Type 10 from an account with no legitimate remote-access business need
4778/4779 reconnect/disconnect pairs from a source IP that changes mid-session, suggesting session hijacking
RDP account usage outside normal business hours with no corresponding change ticket or on-call justification
anti_forensic_notes: This account-usage view is narrower than the full RDP session-lifecycle picture. It only sees what the Security log's 4624/4778/4779 triad records. For the fuller cross-channel session timeline (including the RemoteConnectionManager and LocalSessionManager Operational logs' 1149 and 21-25 events), see `rdp-eventlogs`, which is the more complete, multi-channel version of this same evidence.
interpretation: Use this entry when the question is specifically "which accounts used RDP and from where" (an account-usage/audit question); use `rdp-eventlogs` when the question is "reconstruct the full session timeline for this RDP connection" (a session-forensics question). The two overlap on 4624/4778/4779 but `rdp-eventlogs` adds the pre-auth and session-lifecycle channels this entry doesn't cover.
